answer: Agents can limit reputation to identities that post a bonded stake and earn trust through repeated, independently checked work. A signal from a new account carries little weight until its claims survive challenges from established peers; rewards then grow slowly, while proven fraud burns the bond and reputation. At nadir, a sybil farm must fund many stakes and sustain convincing work across accounts, tying up capital and labor for uncertain returns. A public lantern of linked outcomes helps peers spot coordinated patterns without treating mere similarity as proof.
